To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
LDL and Lovastatin may play a significant role in the metastatic process by facilitating tumor cell migration across microvas-cular endothelium.

(1) LDL-enriched media increases tumor cell transendothelial cell migra-tion across MVEC; (2) Lovastatin suppresses in vitro growth of metastatic colon tumor cells; and (3) Lovastatin reduces the number of liver metastases of colon tumor cells in vivo.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of LDL and Lovastatin on the transendothelial cell adhesion and migration in vitro.
the effects of LDL and Lovastatin on the transendothelial migratory behavior of primary and metastasized tumor cells.
the effects of LDL and the anticholesterol agent Lovastatin on the organ specific metastatic potential of two human colonic adenoca-rinoma cell lines.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
LDL and Lovastatin have no effect on tumor cell adhesion and migration in vitro, however, LDL and Lovastatins have an inhibitory effect on the metastatic process in vivo.
LDL and Lovastatin do have an effect on metastatic behavior, but the effects are organ-specific and cell-type specific.
LDL modulates the metastatic behavior of human colonic tumor cells by increasing tumor cell migration across endothelial cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
LDL and Lovastatin may play a role in metastatic tumor cell migration and may have a potential for the treatment of metastatic disease.
LDL is a potent stimulus of tumor cell migration across endothelium.
LDL increases the transmigration of tumor cells across MVEC, and this process can be inhibited by Lovastatin.
The main takeaway from our work is that
LDL-enriched media increases tumor cell migration across endothelial mon-olayers, and that this effect is not mediated through tumor cell adhesion.
LDL-enriched media increases the transendothelial migratory potential of the tumor cells.
LDL may play an important role in the metastatic behavior of colon adenocarcincoma cells.
